# 4 Ezra Chapter 7 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Latin Vulgate (Codex Sangermanensis) | **Section:** Core apocalypse — The narrow gate and fate of souls

---

**1** And when I had finished speaking these words, the angel who had been sent to me on the previous nights was sent again,

**2** and he said to me: Rise, Ezra, and hear the words I have come to speak to you.

**3** And I said: Speak, my lord. And he said to me: There is a sea set in a wide expanse, so that it is deep and vast,

**4** but it has an entrance set in a narrow place, like a river.

**5** If one desires to go into the sea — whether to look upon it or to navigate it — how can he reach the broad part unless he passes through the narrow?

**6** Again, there is a city built and set on a plain, full of all good things;

**7** but its entrance is narrow and set in a precipitous place, with fire on the right hand and deep water on the left;

**8** and there is only one narrow path between them — between the fire and the water — such that only one person at a time can walk it.

**9** If this city is given to a man as an inheritance, how shall he receive his inheritance unless he passes through the difficulty set before it?

**10** And I said: It is so, lord. And he said to me: So also is the portion of Israel!

**11** For it was for Israel I made the world; and when Adam transgressed my statutes, what was made was judged.

**12** The entrances of this world were made narrow and sorrowful and toilsome — they are few and evil, full of dangers and fraught with great hardships.

**13** But the entrances of the greater world are broad and safe, and yield the fruit of immortality.

**14** Unless therefore the living pass through the difficult and vain experiences, they can never receive those things that have been reserved for them.

**15** Now therefore why are you troubled, seeing that you are mortal? And why are you moved, seeing that you are corruptible?

**16** And why have you not considered in your heart what is to come, rather than what is present?

**17** Then I answered and said: O LORD, my lord, behold, you have ordained in your law that the righteous shall inherit these things, but the ungodly shall perish.

**18** The righteous therefore shall endure straitened things, hoping for spacious things; but those who have done wickedly have suffered the strait and shall not see the spacious.

**19** And he said to me: You are not a judge above God, neither are you more prudent than the Most High.

**20** Let many perish who are now alive rather than that the law of God set before them should be neglected.

**21** For God strictly commanded those who came into the world, when they came, what they should do to live, and what to observe to avoid punishment.

**22** But they were not obedient, and spoke against him; they devised vain thoughts for themselves,

**23** and proposed wicked frauds to themselves; they even declared the Most High does not exist, and they knew not his ways;

**24** they despised his law and rejected his covenants; they have been unfaithful to his statutes and have not performed his works.

**25** Therefore, Ezra, for the empty are empty things, and for the full are the full things.

**26** For behold, the time shall come, and it shall be when the signs I told you about come to pass, that the bride shall appear — and she who has been withdrawn from the earth shall be seen coming forth —

**27** and whoever is delivered from the aforesaid evils shall see my wonders.

**28** For my son the Messiah shall be revealed with those who are with him, and shall gladden those who remain for four hundred years.

**29** And it shall be after those years that my son the Messiah shall die, and all who draw the breath of life.

**30** And the world shall be turned into the primeval silence for seven days, as at the first beginnings; so that no one shall remain.

**31** And it shall be after seven days that the age which is not yet awake shall be roused, and that which is corruptible shall perish.

**32** And the earth shall give up those who are asleep in it, and the dust shall give up those who dwell silently within it, and the storehouses shall restore the souls committed to them.

**33** And the Most High shall appear upon the seat of judgment, and misery shall pass away, and long-suffering shall have an end:

**34** but judgment only shall remain, truth shall stand, and faithfulness shall grow strong;

**35** and recompense shall follow, and the reward shall be manifested; righteous deeds shall awake, and unrighteous deeds shall not sleep.

**36** And the pit of torment shall appear, and over against it the place of refreshment; the furnace of Gehenna shall be made manifest, and over against it the paradise of delight.

**37** Then shall the Most High say to the nations that have been raised from the dead: Look and understand — whom you denied, whom you did not serve, whose commandments you despised!

**38** Look now before you — on this side delight and rest; on that side fire and torments! Thus shall he speak to them on the day of judgment.

**39** There is no day like that day, nor has there ever been — for it is like a day of battle.

**40** And that day shall have no sun, nor moon, nor stars,

**41** nor cloud, nor thunder, nor lightning, nor wind, nor water, nor air, nor darkness, nor evening, nor morning,

**42** nor summer, nor spring, nor heat, nor winter, nor frost, nor cold, nor hail, nor rain, nor dew,

**43** nor noon, nor night, nor dawn, nor shining, nor brightness, nor light — save only the splendor of the glory of the Most High, by which all shall see what has been appointed.

**44** For it shall last as it were for a week of years.

**45** This is my judgment and its prescribed order; and to you alone have I shown these things.

**46** Then I answered and said: O LORD, I said then, and I say now: Blessed are those who live and keep your commandments.

**47** But what of those for whom I prayed? For who among the living has not sinned, and who of those born has not transgressed your covenant?

**48** And now I see that the world to come will bring delight to few, and torment to many.

**49** For an evil heart has grown up in us, which has alienated us from these things and brought us into corruption and into the ways of death, and has shown us the paths of perdition and removed us far from life — and not a few only, but well nigh all who have been created.

**50** And he answered me and said: Hear me, Ezra, and I will instruct you, and admonish you yet again.

**51** For this reason also the Most High created not one world but two.

**52** Inasmuch as you have said that the righteous are not many but few, while the ungodly abound, hear the explanation.

**53** If you have very few precious stones, will you add to their number lead and clay?

**54** And I said: Lord, how could that be?

**55** And he said to me: Not only that, but ask the earth and it will tell you; address it gently and it will speak.

**56** Say to it: You produce gold and silver and copper, and also iron and lead and clay;

**57** but silver is more abundant than gold, and copper than silver, and iron than copper, and lead than iron, and clay than lead.

**58** Judge therefore which things are precious and desirable — those that are abundant or those that are rare?

**59** And I said: O LORD who rules over us, that which is rare is more precious.

**60** And he answered me and said: Weigh within yourself what you have thought; for he who has what is hard to get rejoices more than he who has what is plentiful.

**61** So also will be the judgment I have promised; for I will rejoice over the few who shall be saved, inasmuch as they are those who have made my glory to prevail and through whom my name has been honored.

**62** And I will not grieve over the multitude of those who perish; for they are now like vapor and are become like flame and smoke — they are kindled and burn hotly and are extinguished.

**63** Then I answered and said: O earth, what have you brought forth, if the mind is made out of the dust even as all other created things!

**64** For it were better that the dust itself had not been born, so that the mind might not have come from it, and so that the mind might not now bring us into torment.

**65** But now I know not what is good for us: whether we should be in sorrow or whether we should be glad.

**66** And he answered me and said: Understand that it is better for the creature to come into judgment having sinned than to pass through life without sinning and not be judged.

**67** And I answered and said: I know, O LORD, that the Most High is called merciful, in that he has mercy on those who have not yet come into the world,

**68** and upon those who turn from his law,

**69** and in his long-suffering and compassion he is called merciful forever and ever.

**70** For if he were not merciful, the world could not continue, and the unnumbered people who have sinned would not be able to live.

**71** And he answered me and said: The Most High made this world for the sake of many, but the world to come for the sake of few.

**72** But I tell you a parable, Ezra: as when you ask the earth and it says it gives more clay from which earthen vessels are made, but little dust from which gold comes — so also is the course of the present world.

**73** There is also another thing I will tell you. Do not speak too freely about the Most High;

**74** nor inquire too eagerly into the things that concern you now; for have you not forgotten what it is for a man to be judged and found wanting?

**75** But now do not rejoice over yourself too greatly, nor let it pain you too much.

**76** For on the day of judgment every man shall be judged according to his deeds.

**77** And I said: What then shall be the division among those who have been gathered?

**78** And he answered me and said: This is how it is: the souls of the righteous shall depart from the habitation of the corruptible and shall no longer return to it.

**79** But the souls of the wicked shall see the habitation of those who have been saved; they shall also see the torment that awaits them.

**80** Therefore this is what shall happen: they shall wait seven days of rest, and after those seven days have passed, they shall begin to long for the places they have abandoned.

**81** And this is the order of those who have kept the way of the Most High, when they are separated from their mortal bodies.

**82** During the time they dwelt in them, they labored strenuously to serve the Most High and withstood danger every hour so that the law-giver might be perfected in them.

**83** Therefore this is the teaching concerning them:

**84** First of all they shall see with great joy the glory of him who receives them, for they shall have rest in seven orders.

**85** The first order: they have striven with great effort to overcome the evil thought that was formed with them, that it might not lead them astray from life into death.

**86** The second order: they shall see the wandering of the souls of the wicked and the punishment that awaits them.

**87** The third order: they shall see the witness that he who formed them bears concerning them — that during their lives they kept the law given to them in trust.

**88** The fourth order: they shall understand the rest they now enjoy, being gathered in their chambers and guarded by angels in profound quietness, and the glory that awaits them in the last days.

**89** The fifth order: they shall rejoice that they have escaped what is corruptible and shall inherit what is to come, while beholding also the narrow and toilsome path through which they passed to greatness and blessedness.

**90** The sixth order: it shall be shown to them how their faces are to shine like the sun, and how they are to be made like the light of the stars, being incorruptible from then on.

**91** The seventh order, which is greater than all the aforesaid: they shall exult with confidence, they shall be bold without confusion, and shall be glad without fear, for they hasten to see the face of him whom they served in life and from whom they are to receive their reward when glorified.

**92** This is the order of the souls of the righteous, as henceforth announced; and the aforesaid are the ways of torment that those who would not heed shall suffer hereafter.

**93** And I answered and said: Will time therefore be given to souls after they have been separated from the bodies, to see what you have told me concerning them?

**94** And he said to me: They shall have seven days of freedom, so that during these seven days they may see the things of which you have been told, and afterward they shall be gathered in their habitations.

**95** And I answered and said: If I have found grace before you, show me further — whether on the day of judgment the righteous will be able to intercede for the wicked or to entreat the Most High for them:

**96** fathers for their children, or children for their parents, or brothers for brothers, or relatives for kinsmen, or friends for those most dear.

**97** And he answered me and said: Since you have found grace before me, I will show you this also. The day of judgment is decisive and displays to all the seal of truth;

**98** just as now a father does not send his son, or a son his father, or a master his slave, or a friend his dearest friend, to be ill or sleep or eat or be healed in his stead,

**99** so then no one shall pray for another on that day, nor shall anyone lay a burden on another; for then everyone shall bear his own righteousness and his own wickedness.

**100** Then I answered and said: How then do we find that Abraham prayed first for the people of Sodom, and Moses for our fathers who sinned in the wilderness,

**101** and Joshua after him for Israel in the days of Achan,

**102** and Samuel and David for the destruction, and Solomon for those in the sanctuary,

**103** and Elijah for those who received rain, and for the dead that they might live,

**104** and Hezekiah for the people in the days of Sennacherib, and many others for many?

**105** If therefore the righteous have prayed for the wicked in this present time — when corruption has grown up and unrighteousness increased — why is it not possible in the future as well?

**106** And he answered me and said: This present world is not the end; the fullness of glory has not tarried in it; therefore those who were strong prayed for the weak.

**107** But the day of judgment shall be the end of this present time and the beginning of the immortal time to come, wherein corruption has passed away,

**108** intemperance has come to an end, infidelity has been cut off, righteousness has grown, and faithfulness has sprung up.

**109** Therefore then no one will be able to have mercy on him who has been condemned in the judgment, nor to harm him who is victorious.

**110** Then I answered and said: This is my first and last word: it had been better if the earth had not produced Adam, or else, having produced him, had restrained him from sinning.

**111** For what profit is it for all to live in sorrow now and to expect punishment after death?

**112** O Adam, what have you done? For though it was you who sinned, the fall was not yours alone — it is also ours who are your descendants.

**113** For what profit is it to us if an immortal time is promised to us, whereas we have done the works that bring death?

**114** Or that an everlasting hope is foretold to us, whereas we in our misery have come to a wretched end?

**115** Or that habitations of health and safety are laid up for us, whereas we have lived wickedly?

**116** Or that the glory of the Most High is to protect those who conducted themselves purely, whereas we have walked in most wicked ways?

**117** Or that paradise shall be revealed whose fruit endures incorruptible and therein is abundance and healing — but we shall not enter it,

**118** for we have walked in unpleasant places?

**119** Or that the faces of those who practised abstinence shall shine more than the stars, whereas our faces shall be blacker than darkness?

**120** For we did not think in our lifetime, when we committed iniquity, that after death we should suffer for it.

**121** Then he answered and said: This is the meaning of the contest which every man born on earth wages:

**122** if he is defeated he shall suffer what you have said, but if he is victorious he shall receive what I have said.

**123** For this is the way of which Moses, while he was alive, spoke to the people, saying: Choose life, that you may live.

**124** But they believed him not, neither did they believe the prophets after him, nor even myself who have spoken to them,

**125** so that it shall not be a grief to them that they suffer torment, so much as that they have forsaken the Most High, despised his law, and forsaken his ways.

**126** And those who now dwell in the place of the saved shall not grieve for those who perish, but shall joy over them, because the number of those like themselves is now complete — because the torment of those henceforth preserved is at an end, while the glory of those now justified cannot decrease.

**127** And he answered me and said: When it pleased him to save Israel and to take them to himself, one did not say to another in Egypt that they should have pity on them;

**128** but he sent signs and wonders to rescue them from Egypt and to bring them safely through a difficult way.

**129** So also will I do with those who are now in the end; I will not grieve over the multitude of those who perish.

**130** For they also received freedom, but despised the Most High and scorned his law and forsook his ways.

**131** Moreover they trampled on his righteous ones.

**132** They said in their hearts: There is no God — though knowing that they must die.

**133** For as the things aforesaid shall receive you, so also thirst and torment which are prepared shall receive them; for the Most High did not will that man should perish.

**134** But man himself who was created has defiled the name of him who made him, and has been ungrateful to him who prepared life for him.

**135** And therefore my judgment is now near.

**136** These things I have not shown to all, but only to you and a few like you.

**137** Then I answered and said: O LORD, behold, you have shown me a multitude of signs which you will do in the last time, but you have not shown me when you will do them.

**138** And he answered me and said: Carefully measure the time in your mind; and when you see that a portion of the signs I foretold has passed,

**139** then shall you understand that it is the very time when the Most High is about to visit the world which he has made.

**140** Therefore when earthquakes of peoples, disorder of nations, intrigues of kings, confusion of leaders, and disquietude of princes are seen in the world — then shall you understand, and at that time shall you recognize that the Most High spoke these words to you.
